title: Assignment 14 · Meaning and extrinsic evidence
summary: Meaning and extrinsic evidence. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Pacific Gas & Electric Co. v. G.W. Thomas Drayage & Rigging Co.: California’s contextual approach requires consideration of credible evidence that contract language bears the meaning a party proposes, even when the words initially seem clear.

W.W.W. Associates, Inc. v. Giancontieri: New York enforced a written cancellation right given to either party and refused outside evidence offered to turn it into a right benefiting only the buyer.

Greenfield v. Philles Records, Inc.: The same decision applied New York’s textual approach to a recording agreement and California’s contextual approach to a separate divorce release.

Trident Center v. Connecticut General Life Insurance Co.: A federal court allowed the borrower to present extrinsic evidence under California law despite finding the text clear and criticizing that law’s consequences.

Additional assigned materials: Hall and Elliot, Can AI Fix Bad Rules?.
